memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then they mounted four rows of precious stones on it. The first row was carnelian, chrysolite and beryl; the second row was turquoise, lapis lazuli and emerald; the third row was jacinth, agate and amethyst; the fourth row was topaz, onyx and jasper. They were mounted in gold filigree settings. There were twelve stones, one for each of the names of the sons of Israel, each engraved like a seal with the name of one of the twelve tribes." - Exod 39:10-14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Twelve different stones. Not twelve identical ones.

Carnelian is deep red; emerald is green; amethyst is purple. Different colours, different hardness, different value on any market. God chose variety and set them side by side in gold.

Each stone carried one tribe's name. Reuben was not represented by the same stone as Judah. Each had its own.

That is a good picture of the church. There are different kinds of gifts, but the same Spirit; different kinds of service, but the same Lord (1 Cor 12:4-5). God has never wanted uniformity from His people. He arranged them like a breastpiece — distinct stones held in one setting.

And notice the tribes represented here. Simeon and Levi, who had committed violence at Shechem. Judah, who had failed badly. Reuben, who had disgraced his father. This was not a list of exemplary men. It was a family with a difficult history, and God carried every name.

Whatever your tribe, whatever your temperament, whatever your history — you were not chosen because you matched everyone else. You were set in place as you are.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you wish you were more like someone else in your church?
2. Where does uniformity get mistaken for unity in your thinking?
3. Whose difference have you found hard to appreciate?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You set us together in our variety. Help me value the people who are unlike me. Amen.
